scope_note: DOCS-axis spine for telegram-llm-bot, mined via the docs-surface lens (support/doc sections a mature telegram-llm-bot ships (markdown headings)) from ['AstrBot', 'ChatGPT-Telegram-Bot', 'LangBot', 'nekro-agent']. Does NOT predict project-specific product direction — that is strategy, not completeness. Non-SCOPE axes are advisory in check.py until they beat the generic-baseline control.

required.what: High-level introduction, positioning, capabilities, and why-use sections.
required.day1_tell: Open the main README or docs homepage and verify it has an overview/introduction section explaining what the project is, its main capabilities, and why someone would use it.

required.what: Documented core features, key capabilities, supported use cases, and demos.
required.day1_tell: Open the docs and find a features/capabilities section listing the bot's core features, supported use cases, or demo links/screenshots.

required.what: Fast path for first-time users to launch or deploy the bot.
required.day1_tell: Open the docs and confirm there is a quick-start path that lets a first-time user launch or deploy the bot with minimal steps.

required.what: Multiple deployment options such as Docker, one-click cloud deploy, local source deploy, hosted platforms, or scripts.
required.day1_tell: Open the deployment docs and verify they describe more than one deployment option, such as Docker, cloud deploy, local source deploy, hosted platform, or scripts.

required.what: Instructions for cloning, installing dependencies, bootstrapping backend/frontend, and running locally.
required.day1_tell: Open the developer setup docs and confirm they include clone, dependency installation, backend/frontend bootstrap, and local run commands.

required.what: Environment variables, config files, launch parameters, or runtime configuration guidance.
required.day1_tell: Open the configuration docs and verify there is a reference for environment variables, config files, launch parameters, or runtime settings.

required.what: Messaging platforms, integrations, or bot channels supported by the project.
required.day1_tell: Open the docs and find a supported platforms/channels section naming the messaging platforms, integrations, or bot channels the project supports.

required.what: Supported LLM providers, model backends, TTS, image generation, or AI integrations.
required.day1_tell: Open the docs and verify there is a supported AI/model services section listing LLM providers, model backends, TTS, image generation, or similar integrations.

required.what: Guides for building, debugging, or structuring plugins/extensions/tools.
required.day1_tell: Open the docs and confirm there is a guide for creating, debugging, or structuring plugins, extensions, tools, or custom integrations.

required.what: Repository layout, runtime architecture, sandbox/plugin architecture, or system overview.
required.day1_tell: Open the docs and find an architecture section that explains repository layout, runtime flow, plugin/sandbox architecture, or overall system design.

required.what: Test commands, testing workflow, test steps, or validation expectations.
required.day1_tell: Open the docs and find testing instructions that include test commands, workflow, validation steps, or expected test setup.

required.what: Formatting, linting, pre-commit, code standards, migrations, and quality gates.
required.day1_tell: Open the docs and confirm there are code quality instructions covering formatting, linting, pre-commit hooks, coding standards, migrations, or quality gates.

required.what: How to report issues, submit pull requests, follow contribution rules, and communicate with maintainers.
required.day1_tell: Open CONTRIBUTING.md or contributor docs and verify they explain how to report issues, submit PRs, follow contribution rules, or contact maintainers.

required.what: Pull request checklist, screenshots, change type, implementation details, and maintainer review items.
required.day1_tell: Check the repository for a pull request template and verify it includes a checklist, change type, screenshots, implementation notes, or review guidance.

required.what: License, EULA, copyright, warranties, restrictions, and liability terms.
required.day1_tell: Check the repository for a LICENSE, EULA, or legal section and verify it states license terms, copyright, warranties, restrictions, or liability terms.

required.what: Common issues, workarounds, debugging tips, and operational gotchas.
required.day1_tell: Open the docs and find a troubleshooting section that covers common failures, debugging steps, workarounds, or operational gotchas.

required.what: Frequently asked questions for users or deployers.
required.day1_tell: Open the docs and verify there is an FAQ section with common questions and answers for users, deployers, or developers.

required.what: Release versions, changelog, preview/stable channels, and update notes.
required.day1_tell: Check the repository or docs for a changelog/releases page and verify it lists versions, release notes, update history, or preview/stable channels.

required.what: Community links, support channels, sponsors, contributors, and star history.
required.day1_tell: Open the README or docs and verify there are community/support links such as Discord, Slack, forum, sponsors, contributors, or star history.

required.what: Documentation duplicated or localized across multiple languages.
required.day1_tell: Open the docs and verify the same documentation is available in more than one language or includes localized language folders/pages.

optional.what: API references, response formats, SDK/runtime APIs, or developer-facing interface docs.
optional.day1_tell: Open the docs and verify there is API documentation with endpoints, SDK/runtime APIs, request/response formats, or developer interfaces.

optional.what: Community behavior expectations and enforcement policy.
optional.day1_tell: Check the repository or docs for a Code of Conduct and verify it states community behavior expectations and enforcement/reporting policy.
